To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of parallel spring elements at select joints in a bipedal walker reduces dissipated power and improves locomotive efficiency.
parallel elastic elements at the hip and ankle of a bipedal walking robot can reduce power consumption and improve efficiency.

1) the addition of parallel springs to a bipedal walker can improve efficiency by 30% to 50%, 2) this is achieved through a reduction in the dissipated power of the actuation, and 3) the addition of springs to the hip roll and ankle joints is predicted to be the most effective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to improve the efficiency of a legged robot by reducing the amount of power required to perform locomotive tasks.
the development of a bipedal walker capable of human-like locomotive efficiency.
the design, control and implementation of parallel springs to improve the locomotive efficiency of the STEPPR bipedal robot.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of parallel springs at the hip roll and ankle joints of a bipedal walker is predicted to reduce cost of transport by up to 50%.
the use of parallel stiffness to reduce dissipated power is a promising approach for improving the efficiency of legged robots.
the addition of parallel spring elements to the STEPPR robot is a very promising method to improve locomotive efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are designing and building a bipedal walking robot to explore the use of parallel springs in the design and control of efficient walking robots.
parallel elastic elements can be designed to provide substantial energetic improvements in bipedal robots.
we are using parallel stiffness to achieve efficient locomotion with the Sandia robot.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parallel stiffness, when added to select joints in a robot, can significantly improve locomotive efficiency.
parallel springs can be used to improve the energy efficiency of legged robots by reducing the power dissipated in actuated joints.
adding parallel elastic elements at the ankle and hip roll joints of a bipedal walker is predicted to significantly reduce the metabolic energy consumption of the system.
